label: Tutorial: Add rules
description: Steps of the Tutorial button on the Add rules page (endpoint rule.rule). A step: target (CSS selector, empty = centred card), title, text (blank line = new paragraph, **bold**, `code`), roles (optional: anonymous, user, member, admin, perm:<key>), demo (rule / bundle: example shown when the target is missing, e.g. an empty list).

steps.title: Seven ways to add rules
steps.text: Each tab is a way in. Whatever you choose, every rule is checked with its format's own validator before it is saved, and gets the default tags `tlp:clear` and `pap:clear`.

steps.title: By hand — 1. Identity
steps.text: The **title** (unique on Rulezet) and the **format**. The format decides how the content is checked.

steps.title: By hand — 2. Classification
steps.text: **Licence** (can others reuse it?), **CVEs** it detects, **ATT&CK techniques** and **tags**. They make the rule findable in the filters and on the CVE and ATT&CK pages.

steps.title: By hand — 3. Content
steps.text: Paste the rule. A rule that does not compile is refused, with the error and the line shown.

steps.title: Paste a whole file
steps.text: Paste many rules at once: Rulezet splits them, reads their metadata (author, references, description) and shows each one before creating them. Rules in error are listed, the others are created.

steps.title: From a Git repository
steps.text: The URL of a GitHub, GitLab, Gitea… repository and a branch: every rule found is imported, with a link back to its file. The repository is remembered, so its rules can be **updated** later in one sync.

steps.title: From a zip file
steps.text: Upload an archive of rule files: same checks as above, one rule per file (or per rule in a file).

steps.title: YARA editor
steps.text: A full YARA editor: live syntax checks, autocompletion, rules that use other rules, templates, a Try panel on a sample, and tests on sample sets before saving.
